suggestions.expectation: The brief's Session line states one of the three outcomes and the disk agrees …
suggestions.reason: This run declared `joined` while doing `none` on disk (nothing appended, no file). The expectation catches the wrong word, which is right, but a `none`-on-disk / `joined`-in-brief mismatch is a distinct failure mode worth naming explicitly: the Session line must match what the tool was actually asked to do (a join is `bun run session append --session SES-NNN` or at least a stated `--session` binding for future commits), not a promise.

suggestions.expectation: brief.md contains a line starting with 'read in full:' … and transcript.md shows each of those was read to its last line
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is written by the executor after the fact; a run that asserts 'end reached' without doing it passes identically. The line-range/wc -l cross-check I did is the only independent oracle, and it only works because the executor volunteered line counts. Consider requiring the transcript to quote the last line of each file (checkable against the fixture) or grading from the raw tool log.

No expectation names the red gate. The run context says a5ff930 lacking an entry is the expected state and the point is whether it was reported; this run did report it ('gate NOT ready — a5ff930 has no entry') but only expectation 6's generic 'state of the tree … as findings' covers it. Add: 'Findings line reports the gate as NOT ready naming a5ff930, and the run does not append/fill an entry to make it green.'

Expectation 1's 1,600-char bound is looser than the old skill's ~1,200 and the new skill's template; both arms will pass it trivially. If the new skill has a stated bound, grade against that so the length check discriminates.

eval_feedback.overall: The expectations discriminated well here: six pass on verified disk/transcript evidence and the one failure (declared join to a session whose Goal is not this work) is a genuine defect of the baseline behaviour, not a technicality. Main gap is that read-to-end evidence rests on the executor's self-report.
